title: Multicolour Ramsey number R(3,5,5), lower bound
statement: Find a colouring of the edges of K_n with 3 colours 0..2 in which colour c holds no complete graph K_(S_(c+1)), for (S_1, ..., S_3) = (3,5,5); it shows R(3,5,5) > n. The best known lower bound is R(3,5,5) >= 139, so a colouring of K_138 is known and one of K_139 or more would improve it.
submission: Text file: the n x n colour matrix, one line of n characters per vertex; the character in row i, column j (i != j) is the colour of the edge {i,j}, a digit from 0 to r-1 (colour c must avoid K_(S_(c+1))), symmetric; diagonal characters are ignored (write 0 or -). n <= 2048 is practical.
score: n, the number of vertices of the colouring; it proves R(3,5,5) >= n + 1 (larger is better)

best_known.source: R(3,5,5) >= 139: [Ex17] in Small Ramsey Numbers rev. 18 (24 Apr 2026), Table XIb; read 8 Nov 2026

provenance.keeper: Small Ramsey Numbers (S. Radziszowski), EJC Dynamic Survey DS1
